Text.homeTitle: GOUI — Lightweight Golang GUI Framework, No cgo
Text.homeDescription: Build lightweight, modern desktop apps in Go with GOUI. A native Golang GUI framework for Windows, macOS and Linux, without cgo, GCC or a browser engine.
Text.startTitle: Go GUI Tutorial — Build Your First GOUI Desktop App
Text.startDescription: Create your first Go desktop GUI with GOUI v0.1.0. Install the module, build a counter app with CGO_ENABLED=0, and learn platform runtime requirements.
Text.eyebrow: A NATIVE GUI FRAMEWORK FOR GO
Text.heroLead: GOUI is a lightweight Golang GUI framework for building modern desktop applications. Write your interface and your logic in Go—not in a browser engine.
Text.heroNote: No cgo. No GCC. No browser engine.
Text.screenshotCaption: Real GOUI demo · light and dark styles · three desktop platforms
Text.screenshotAlt: GOUI demo showing desktop controls, modern styling and a sidebar on
Text.introTitle: A desktop toolkit, not a web stack.
Text.introLead: Use Go's toolchain, embed your assets, and ship a focused native application. GOUI handles the parts a desktop interface needs, without becoming an all-purpose platform SDK.
Text.reasonOneText: Build with CGO_ENABLED=0. Native APIs are loaded at runtime, so building your application requires no C/C++ compiler or development headers.
Text.reasonTwoText: Windows and Linux applications can run as a single executable. On macOS, wrap the binary in an .app for identity, icons and signing. Native system libraries are still required.
Text.reasonThreeText: Light/dark styles and accent colors meet native window chrome, text layout, IME, clipboard and file dialogs. Choose declarative views or imperative widgets.
Text.featuresLead: The first release provides the foundations and controls for small desktop apps, from utilities and note-taking tools to data-oriented workspaces.
Text.architectureTitle: Use only the layers you need.
Text.architectureLead: Learned from GTK4, Flutter, Qt, Avalonia and SwiftUI. Adapted to Go, rather than copied wholesale.
Text.layerUI: Declarative views and explicit update coordination
Text.layerGUI: Widgets, layouts, painting, events, focus and signals
Text.layerPlatform: Native windows, input, drawing and typography
Text.codeLead: Views are ordinary Go values. State updates request a coalesced rebuild; you decide how to structure your application.
Text.copyFailed: Copy unavailable. Select the code and copy it manually.
Text.downloadTitle: A real app. A small download.
Text.downloadLead: The demo brings together editing, data views, detachable tabs, overlays, graphics and system integration. Try light/dark modes, accent colors and eight UI languages.
Text.downloadNotes: Linux: make the binary executable with chmod +x. macOS: extract the ZIP and open GOUI Demo.app; the bundle is ad-hoc signed, not notarized. ZIP size is not executable size.
Text.measurementTitle: Lightweight, with the numbers in context.
Text.measurementText: With Go 1.25.8, CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath and stripped symbols, the documented minimal app builds are 4.46–4.75 MiB. Linux/X11 Software 1x reference measurements report 28.6 MiB PSS for a minimal app and 46.2 MiB for the demo. These are development measurements—not release download sizes, Go heap sizes, or promises for every platform.
Text.platformIntro: No cgo is a build property, not a claim that the application has no runtime dependencies.
Text.windowsText: Windows x64 · Win32 windows · DirectWrite text · Direct2D, OpenGL or Software drawing.
Text.macText: macOS Apple Silicon · AppKit windows · Core Text · OpenGL or Software drawing. Signing and notarization remain application distribution steps.
Text.linuxText: Linux x64 · X11 · Pango/Cairo text · OpenGL or Software drawing. Needs native X11, GL, GLib, Fontconfig, Pango/Cairo and GTK runtime libraries. Wayland sessions require XWayland; behavior must be checked on the target desktop.
Text.limitations: v0.1.0 is a first release: APIs are still evolving. Touch, additional platforms and window systems, more application controls, and continued performance work are on the roadmap.
Text.ctaText: Start with a small window. Grow into the layers and controls your application actually needs.
Text.footerText: Open-source native desktop tools for Go.
Text.footerAttribution: GOUI artwork adapts the Go gopher by Renee French (CC BY 4.0).
Text.startHeading: A Go GUI, in a few steps.
Text.startLead: Build a small counter application with GOUI v0.1.0. The same interface code targets Windows, macOS and Linux; no C/C++ compiler is needed.
Text.prereqText: Install Go 1.24 or newer and use a supported desktop environment. The published demo targets Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon and Linux x64/X11. Linux also needs the native runtime libraries described below.
Text.stepOneText: Pin the first release so this tutorial does not silently move to a newer API.
Text.stepTwoText: Save the following as main.go. The Modern stylesheet follows system settings; clicking the button updates the state and rebuilds the view.
Text.stepThreeText: On Linux or macOS, use the following commands. Run the application on your desktop, not in a session without a display.
Text.powershellText: Use -H=windowsgui to build without a console window. Omit that flag while debugging if you want to see terminal output.
Text.stepFourText: ui is the declarative adapter; gui provides imperative widgets; widgets contains additional controls. Application behavior belongs to your app, not the view declarations.
Text.packagingText: An ordinary go build is enough to create the executable. The optional cmd/goui tool prepares Windows icon/version resources, macOS .app metadata and icons, and Linux desktop/icon resources from goui.toml. It does not remove system runtime requirements.

Text.nextTitle: You're ready to build something small.
Text.nextText: Try the demo, browse the examples, then implement the application that matters to you. v0.1.0 is a starting point, with APIs still evolving.

Features.Title: Everyday controls
Features.Text: Buttons, labels, icons, menus, dropdowns, check/radio buttons, switches and linear or circular progress indicators.

Features.Title: Editing that feels native
Features.Text: Unicode text editing, CJK IME, selection, undo/redo, clipboard, keyboard shortcuts and Tab focus navigation.

Features.Title: Data and flexible layouts
Features.Text: Constraint-based boxes, wrapping, scrolling, overlays, split views, virtualized lists, trees and tables with custom cells.

Features.Title: Multi-window workspaces
Features.Text: Reorder tabs, transfer them between windows, detach into a new window, and use native drag and drop.

Features.Title: Graphics and appearance
Features.Text: Style-aware SVG icons, light/dark modes, accent colors, HiDPI, transparency, shadows and frame-driven animation.

Features.Title: System and developer tools
Features.Text: File dialogs, file-access credentials, timers, system settings, URL/file opening, build tooling and opt-in semantic UI inspection.

FAQs.Title: Is GOUI a web wrapper?
FAQs.Text: No. GOUI draws widgets through native graphics backends and uses native text layout. It does not embed a browser engine.

FAQs.Title: Do I need GCC or cgo?
FAQs.Text: No C/C++ compiler is required to build your app. GOUI supports CGO_ENABLED=0 and binds native libraries at runtime. Runtime library requirements still apply.

FAQs.Title: Can I cross-compile?
FAQs.Text: Supported targets can be built with the Go toolchain without cgo. Packaging, signing and actual platform validation are separate steps; a successful build does not verify native behavior.

FAQs.Title: Is everything in v0.1.0 stable?
FAQs.Text: No. This release is intended for building small applications and gathering practical feedback. Public APIs continue to evolve; pin a version and review changes when upgrading.
